text: Why does Chapter 14 introduce testing alongside decomposition rather than as a separate topic?
choices: Because untested code cannot be safely decomposed without changing behaviour.
Because a method small enough to name is a method small enough to test, so the two disciplines make each other cheap.
Because tests must be written before the decomposition to drive the design.
Because test frameworks require methods to be static, which decomposition encourages.
explanation: The relationship runs both ways and is worth noticing. A hundred-line method with six responsibilities is hard to test because reaching any one of them requires setting up all six; six named methods are each testable in isolation. Chapter 30 makes the same argument about interfaces — everything you move out of the view becomes testable, and everything you leave in effectively is not.
